newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rupee ends up in kerb, seen stable.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee closed 0.02 rupee up at 42.58 to the dollar in kerb trade on Thursday, but dealers said they expected it to stabilise when the market reopens after the Friday weekend.
A dealer at ARY International Exchange said interest in the Iraqi dinar, steady at 2.50 rupees, had ebbed after speculative activity on Wednesday ahead of an U.N.-Iraqi oil-for-food deal.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on October 22, was 40.1200/40.3206 to the dollar. The premium on forex bearer certificates closed steady at 6.40 percent.
